elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The successor carve-out does not cover ordinary assignments by IBM to an affiliate. The MSL Related Company provision applies only to MSL and still requires IBM's consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The first sentence permits either Party, including IBM, to assign to a successor in a merger upon notice, and the consent requirement applies only “Otherwise.”

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The first sentence expressly permits either Party to assign to a successor in an acquisition upon notice without consent.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The first sentence expressly permits either Party to assign to a successor in a sale of substantially all of its assets upon notice without consent.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: Although other MSL assignments require IBM's approval, MSL may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets on notice alone.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to a Vendor assignment.
elements.evidence: The general approval requirement states that approval shall not be unreasonably withheld, and the MSL Related Company provision separately applies the same standard to IBM's consent.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor, even with Customer consent.
elements.evidence: The clause contains no prohibition against assignment to an IBM competitor.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right upon Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: No operative language grants MSL a termination right arising from IBM's change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The first sentence permits either Party to make such an assignment, and the consent requirement applies only “Otherwise.”

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The first sentence expressly includes assignment to a successor in an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The first sentence expressly includes assignment to a successor in a sale of substantially all of the assigning Party's assets.

elements.element: Customer must give Vendor written notice of a permitted successor assignment.
elements.evidence: The successor assignment right is conditioned on written notice to the other Party.

elements.element: Vendor may assign without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The first sentence gives either Party, including MSL, this right, and the consent requirement applies only “Otherwise.”

elements.element: Vendor may assign without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The first sentence expressly includes assignment by either Party to a successor in an acquisition.

elements.element: Vendor may assign without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.
elements.evidence: The first sentence expressly includes assignment by either Party to a successor in a sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Vendor must give Customer written notice of a permitted successor assignment.
elements.evidence: The successor assignment right requires written notice to the other Party; the later MSL-specific provision also requires immediate notice for specified transactions.

elements.element: Customer assignments outside the successor carve-out require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: The second sentence provides that otherwise neither Party may assign without the other Party's prior written approval.

elements.element: Vendor may not unreasonably withhold consent to other Customer assignments.
elements.evidence: The mutual approval requirement states that approval shall not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor assignments outside the successor carve-out require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: The second sentence requires the other Party's prior written approval for assignments outside the successor carve-out.

elements.element: Customer may not unreasonably withhold consent to other Vendor assignments.
elements.evidence: The mutual approval requirement states that approval shall not be unreasonably withheld; the MSL Related Company provision also expressly applies that standard to IBM.

result.reason: The operative language fully implements the fallback but not the preferred position: IBM lacks an affiliate carve-out, MSL receives a consent-free successor carve-out, and there is no competitor prohibition. The redline is not minimal and does not fully preserve unrelated intent because the new reasonableness limitation applies not only to other assignments but also to transfers and subcontracting, changing the original approval standard for subcontracting beyond the stated fallback. Drafting quality is also reduced by the orphaned “MSL shall” fragment and redundant MSL-specific provisions.
